If a shallow foundation is adequate, it is usually the simplest and cheapest solution. A deep foundation is needed if the bearing stratum is deep, the settlement with a shallow foundation is unacceptable, scour or sliding is a threat, or if it is more economical overall.

In a place with difficult access and limited headroom, the micropile is made with a small rig and transfers the load to the deeper, better layer (underpinning). Jet grouting is also suitable for strengthening foundations and deepening the foundation level, in any soil.

The diaphragm wall is watertight and stiff, it is built relatively free of noise and vibration, it needs no groundwater lowering, and it can be part of the permanent structure – the side wall, even the foundation, of the underground car park.
Well foundation – or a short bored pile

The well foundation is economical if the bearing stratum is not too deep, and especially with high groundwater, when the foundation level has to be taken below the water table. Today it is made as an excavated foundation with a recovered steel casing – but a short bored pile is often its competitor.
Driven precast, CFA or screw pile

Without a vibration limit, the driven precast pile may also come into question – if there is no rock, hard clay, cemented or blocky layer in its path – and the displacement even compacts the soil. The final decision is made by the soil, the load and the economy.
